bug_semantics: A user who can trigger an action can submit arbitrary StartAction argument names and values. The vulnerable filter retains every caller-controlled name beginning with `ot_`, although only `ot_executionTrackingId` and `ot_username` are legitimate system arguments and those two are overwritten by the server. Any other `ot_` name survives, is skipped by type checking because validation iterates only over the action's configured argument definitions, remains available as `.Arguments.ot_*` during template rendering, and is converted by `buildEnv` into an unvalidated uppercased environment variable for the executed command. This permits environment and template-context pollution with attacker-chosen values.
flaw_origin: Commit 4bbd2eab153287dc744ad061c58af7693f0c3ddc added `filterToDefinedArgumentsOnly` while fixing GHSA-49gm-hh7w-wfvf, but deliberately preserved every key with `strings.HasPrefix(k, "ot_")` so that system arguments injected before filtering would survive. That broad prefix exception, rather than an allowlist of the two server-owned keys or injection after filtering, first wrote the advisory's prefix-specific bypass. Its parent already passed all undefined arguments because it had no such filter, so this commit narrowed the older generic exposure but is still the smallest commit that introduced the exact vulnerable filter mechanism identified by GHSA-prj9-97mp-mwh2.
ai_marker: absent: the raw commit object for 4bbd2eab153287dc744ad061c58af7693f0c3ddc has author `jamesread <contact@jread.com>`, committer `jamesread <contact@jread.com>`, and the sole message `security: GHSA-49gm-hh7w-wfvf`; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot marker/trailer.
evidence: First-party repository advisory https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/security/advisories/GHSA-prj9-97mp-mwh2 and its API record https://api.github.com/repos/OliveTin/OliveTin/security-advisories/GHSA-prj9-97mp-mwh2 identify `service/internal/executor/executor.go`: `keepArgument`/the `ot_` exception, the two-key `injectSystemArgs`, and `buildEnv`; they describe unvalidated `ot_*` arguments reaching environment variables and template context and reference fix https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/commit/ebffd9f040f791208aee1db2e5a8aecd1e3e603d.

At 4bbd2eab153287dc744ad061c58af7693f0c3ddc, `service/internal/api/api.go` lines 111-129 copies every caller-supplied StartAction argument into `ExecutionRequest.Arguments`. In `service/internal/executor/executor.go` lines 657-739, `stepParseArgs` injects the two known system keys before `filterToDefinedArgumentsOnly`, while the newly added conditional `if _, ok := definedNames[k]; ok || strings.HasPrefix(k, "ot_")` preserves arbitrary additional `ot_` keys.

At that same BIC, `service/internal/executor/arguments.go` lines 85-101 validates only `req.Binding.Action.Arguments` and passes the full surviving map to `tpl.ParseTemplateWithActionContext`; `service/internal/tpl/templates.go` lines 121-140 exposes the map as `Arguments`; and `service/internal/executor/executor.go` lines 849-862 and 911 pass every map entry through `buildEnv` to the command environment.

`git log -L` traced the current `keepArgument` body through extraction commit 38d6b57077028300a0c9bee9176a75dd4a44ba83 (`chore: codefmt`) to the inline addition in 4bbd2eab153287dc744ad061c58af7693f0c3ddc. `git log -S 'strings.HasPrefix(k, "ot_")'` likewise identifies 4bbd2eab153287dc744ad061c58af7693f0c3ddc as the addition and 38d6b57077028300a0c9bee9176a75dd4a44ba83 only as its later helper extraction, so the refactor is not the BIC.

Direct-parent verification: 4bbd2eab153287dc744ad061c58af7693f0c3ddc has the single parent 1db6509288bb356c6b9128a2318c91fc16e80d83. `git grep -n -F 'strings.HasPrefix(k, "ot_")' 1db6509288bb356c6b9128a2318c91fc16e80d83 -- service/internal/executor/executor.go` returned no match, and the BIC diff adds the entire filter and vulnerable conditional. The parent instead had no undefined-argument filter, explaining why older releases could exhibit the broader pollution impact even though the exact prefix-exception line begins here.

Fix verification: single-parent commit ebffd9f040f791208aee1db2e5a8aecd1e3e603d directly changes `service/internal/executor/executor.go` so `keepArgument` returns only `ok`, moves system-argument injection after filtering, validates the two system values, and adds reserved-prefix configuration validation in `service/internal/config/sanitize.go`. Its direct parent 41612c6bc6a8a6424e27e6a66fb0dae30524c768 contains `return ok || strings.HasPrefix(name, "ot_")` at line 738; the fix contains `return ok` at line 740.

Version cross-check: the reviewed global GitHub advisory API https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-prj9-97mp-mwh2 declares `< 0.0.0-20260531214440-ebffd9f040f7` vulnerable and `0.0.0-20260531214440-ebffd9f040f7` first patched, exactly naming the fix commit. Repository history shows 3000.10.1 is the first tag containing the exact BIC, 3000.13.0 still has the vulnerable line, and 3000.14.0 is the first tag containing ebffd9f040f791208aee1db2e5a8aecd1e3e603d and has the fixed `return ok`; every later inspected release tag also contains the fix.

The repository-advisory endpoint separately reports `<= 2025.03.07` and an empty patched-version field, which conflicts with the later reviewed global GHSA normalization. The commit and tag trees resolve the source boundary: 3000.13.0 is vulnerable and 3000.14.0 contains the direct fix; pre-BIC releases had the broader all-undefined-arguments behavior rather than the later prefix-specific filter bypass.

BIC-only AI check used `git cat-file commit 4bbd2eab153287dc744ad061c58af7693f0c3ddc`: its raw object contains a human author and committer, one parent, and no trailers or AI/bot attribution. No PR text, later refactor, or fix-commit metadata was used for attribution.
reasoning: The advisory's causal chain is present in the source: StartAction accepts caller-controlled argument pairs, the BIC's new filter treats an entire reserved-looking prefix as trusted, only two exact names are replaced by server values, validation enumerates configured arguments rather than all surviving map entries, and the surviving map feeds both templates and the child environment. History distinguishes the true origin from a later mechanical extraction: 38d6b57077028300a0c9bee9176a75dd4a44ba83 merely moved the already-vulnerable inline condition into `keepArgument`, whereas 4bbd2eab153287dc744ad061c58af7693f0c3ddc first authored it and its direct parent lacks it. Although the parent was more broadly permissive, that does not make the later refactor the BIC; 4bbd2eab153287dc744ad061c58af7693f0c3ddc is the smallest commit that first wrote the advisory's specific prefix-whitelist flaw. The direct fix ebffd9f040f791208aee1db2e5a8aecd1e3e603d removes the prefix exception, filters before injecting narrowly defined system values, validates those values, and reserves the prefix in configuration. Tag membership independently brackets the exact implementation from 3000.10.1 through 3000.13.0 and the fix from 3000.14.0. Finally, the BIC's raw commit object has only human jamesread authorship/committer identity and no AI marker, so under the required BIC-only attribution rule the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
